name: Malformation of the Cerebellar Hemispheres

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Radiological and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Cerebellar Malformations

criteria.description: MRI evidence of hypoplasia or dysgenesis localized to one or both cerebellar hemispheres
Presence of cerebellar ataxia manifesting as gait instability or limb dysmetria
Exclusion of acquired cerebellar lesions or metabolic causes by clinical and laboratory evaluation
Supportive finding of delayed motor milestones consistent with cerebellar dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: MRI confirmation of cerebellar hemisphere malformation plus clinical evidence of cerebellar dysfunction with exclusion of acquired causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on neuroimaging combined with clinical neurological assessment.

pathognomonic.notes: Identified via MRI as hallmark structural anomaly
searchTerms: small cerebellar hemisphere on one side
one cerebellar half smaller than normal
uncoordinated movement in one arm or leg

pathognomonic.symptomName: Dysmetria affecting upper and lower limbs
searchTerms: lack of precision in arm and leg movements
balance problems with broad feet placement

rare.symptomName: Hydrocephalus secondary to posterior fossa malformation
searchTerms: fluid buildup in brain due to brain malformation
brain swelling from posterior fossa defect
hydrocephalus caused by back brain abnormality
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

laboratory: Normal metabolic and infectious workup excluding acquired causes
imaging: MRI showing unilateral or bilateral cerebellar hemisphere hypoplasia or dysgenesis
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; some cases linked to developmental gene variants
other: Clinical neurological examination revealing cerebellar signs

distinguishingFeatures: Enlarged posterior fossa with cystic dilation of the fourth ventricle
Hypoplasia of the vermis rather than isolated hemispheric involvement
Associated respiratory irregularities and oculomotor apraxia

redFlags: Onset of seizures or cranial nerve deficits
references: Parisi MA. Cerebellar malformations: clinical and molecular features. Am J Med Genet C Semin Med Genet. 2009.
Barkovich AJ, et al. Classification system for malformations of cortical development. Neurology. 2012.
